The facts describe two sets: first part (1) and (2) describe theft of cash by swapping real cash with counterfeit money while purchasing cigarettes. That's essentially theft (盗窃) because he took the victim's real money by deception? Actually it's a form of fraud: using counterfeit money to pay and taking back the victim's real money. That's akin to fraud (诈骗) or theft? The description says "盗走" the victim's real money after swapping with counterfeit. That's theft (secret taking). The prosecution also charges "诈骗罪" for the later act (selling cigarettes and paying with counterfeit money). The first part also could be considered fraud (using counterfeit money to obtain goods). But they label as theft? In earlier examples, similar scenario of swapping cash with counterfeit was labeled as 盗窃; also they added 掩饰、隐瞒犯罪所得、犯罪所得收益 for concealment. That's theft of cash (盗窃) and also fraud (诈骗) for the later act. The text says "二、诈骗罪" for the third incident. So we have both theft and fraud. Also possibly "伪造、变造、买卖国家机关公文、证件、印章"? No, counterfeit money is not a state document; it's counterfeit currency, which is not listed. There's no specific crime for counterfeit money in list. So we stick with 盗窃 and 诈骗. Also maybe "掩饰、隐瞒犯罪所得、犯罪所得收益" because he concealed? Not mentioned. In earlier example they added that label when there was concealment of proceeds. Here not explicit. So answer: [罪名]盗窃;诈骗<eoa>.
